newsitem.title: GERMANY: Snapshots of Krupp and Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Snapshots of Krupp and Thyssen.

text.p: Should German industrial group Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp be successful in its bid for rival Thyssen AG, it would create one of the world's largest steel and engineering conglomerates.
Here is a snapshot of the two companies and details of their main business activities:
(All figures in millions of marks unless stated)
NOTE - Krupp figures are preliminary for the 1996 calendar year. Thyssen figures are final for the business year to September 30, 1996.
Thyssen AG has three main business divisions.

Thyssen Industrie AG groups its capital goods and engineering businesses which range from manufacturing lifts and escalators to automotive components and rail transport technology, such as the Transrapid magnetic-levitation train.
Thyssen Stahl AG is Germany's biggest steel maker.

Thyssen Handelsunion AG is the trading and services division and has been the umbrella for the company's diversification into telecommunications with its stake in the E-Plus Mobilfunk mobile phone group and other activities.

Thyssen's largest single customer is the automobile industry, which accounts for 18 percent of total sales, followed by trading, steel, components for the construction industry and engineering and plant construction.
Krupp is broken up into six main business divisions - engineering, plant construction, automotive components, industrial processing, steel and trading and services.

The largest division in terms of sales is steel, which had turnover of 10.3 billion marks in 1996, followed by trading and services with sales of 5.6 billion marks and automotive components and industrial processing, which each generated turnover of three billion marks last year.
